reason: A keeps the reading order (brand, GET A GIFT headline, subcopy, Christmas line) in a pink panel on the left with the photo on the right, but everything is crammed into a narrow column. The brand name, 'Only this Christmas' and the URL are tiny, the stars are oversized next to them, the dashed dividers float out of alignment, and the URL is stranded off to the right. B is broken: 'GET A GIFT' is shrunk to a minor label, and the supporting copy 'with your next cup of coffee' becomes the largest text and sits directly on the busy sweater and mug photo, as do 'Only this Christmas' and the URL. The gift icons are blown up into the dominant element, and stray dashed lines float at the edges.

A is a reasonable two-column banner: the photo is on the left and the copy is centered in the heart on the right. But the white heart now sits on a white background, so it reads as a faint grey outline and loses the original's layered overlap. The headline is also small for the large panel, and the photo has margins on three sides but touches nothing at the bottom. B keeps the heart overlapping the photo, but it leaves roughly the right 40% of the canvas as dead white space. The heart is cut off at the bottom edge, and 'Nothing Feels As Good' runs past the heart's edge onto the photo and background, so the layout is lopsided and looks unfinished.

A: the photo shrinks to a small thumbnail jammed against the left edge, and the white heart shape that held the text is gone. The headline is small and floats in a wide empty white band, so the design reads like a plain text strip rather than the photo-led original. B is worse: the white heart shape is left on white as a faint, empty, broken-looking outline cut off from the copy, the URL is pushed off as a tiny scrap on the far right, and the photo sits as a small boxed thumbnail. B's pieces are scattered with no grouping. Its headline is slightly larger, but that doesn't make up for this.

A: the white heart shape now sits on a white background as a ghostly empty outline in the middle of the banner, which looks like a rendering mistake. The photo is shrunk to a small thumbnail floating with uneven margins, and the URL is stranded at the far right, away from the headline, so the banner reads as four scattered fragments. B: the URL sits under the headline as one group, and the photo is anchored to the left edge, but the heart survives only as a faint broken outline behind 'Silk Linen'. The right ~40% of the canvas is dead white, the photo is tiny, the text is small for the format, and the original's text-on-heart-over-image identity is lost in both.

A breaks the design. The photo stops about 60px short of the right edge. A huge dead white band fills the middle. The white heart now sits on a white background, so it shows only as a faint outline and no longer works as a cutout over the bed. The headline and URL are pushed to the bottom, cut off from the image. B is just the original shrunk and letterboxed, with large empty white bands top and bottom and smaller, hard-to-read text, so it doesn't use the tall format. Still, the heart-over-photo composition, the hierarchy and the brand feel all come through intact.

A: 'J'adore Paris' floats alone in the top empty area, cut off from its divider rule. 'LAVANDER' sits on a stray line above the label frame instead of inside it. The illustrations are broken into scattered pieces (the sack and bowl drift at the bottom), but the hierarchy and the illustrated feel mostly survive. B: the label frame is empty, holding only orphaned divider rules. All the text is left-aligned outside the frame, and 'HOMEMADE LOTION' is centred awkwardly under it. The illustrations shrink to a tiny strip, leaving huge dead space above and below, so the design's identity is lost.

A: the body copy is set as large as the headline, so the two compete for attention, and it wraps badly ('real' sits alone on a line). The teal line and contact block are crammed against the lower dashes and the bottom edge, the URL nearly touches both sides, and left-aligned headline and teal text sit next to centred body and contact text. B: the headline-to-body size steps match the original and the vertical spacing is more even, but the contact/URL text has shrunk to an illegible ~5px. B repeats A's left-versus-centred alignment mix and leaves large empty gaps around the teal line.

Both crop away the brush/palette frame that defined the original and add an odd pale translucent band with hard seams across the middle. A keeps the three boxes at their original small size, so the title block floats in a large empty band. B scales the boxes up for better presence, but the KIT box is narrower and offset from the two above, and it runs past the band's lower seam. Its gaps are also uneven, and the off-centre text inside each box is more obvious at this size. That makes B look sloppier, so A is marginally better.

A reverses the message to 'MAKEUP TRAVEL', and 'KIT' has lost its white box: it sits clipped, black-on-dark over the busy brush photo and is almost unreadable. B keeps the reading order TRAVEL, MAKEUP, KIT, but its white bars run into each other and look misaligned (MAKEUP is pushed against the right of its bar), 'KIT' also floats boxless on the image with poor contrast, and the tiny text and cropped photo make it look like a squashed strip, not a redesigned banner.

A scrambles the title into 'MAKEUP TRAVEL … KIT': MAKEUP comes before TRAVEL, the first two words are tiny side-by-side pills far from KIT, and a big dead gap sits between them. On top of that, a visible lighter background band cuts across the middle, and most of the makeup imagery from the original is gone. B keeps the TRAVEL/MAKEUP/KIT stack in order and at a readable size, but it shares the same mismatched background band. Its KIT bar runs edge to edge and is taller than the other two, which breaks the series of matching pills, and MAKEUP sits off-centre in its bar.

A: the X, slash marks and circle are pulled away from the panel and dropped onto the busy photo, where they float without purpose; the circle sits on top of a person's hands. The panel is narrow, so the type is very small ('Join WADE team' and 'WE CREATE' are hard to read), and the panel's top and bottom are cropped by the canvas edges. B: the X, slashes and circle stay on the panel corners, as in the original, so the framing reads as one deliberate unit. The type is a little larger, though the corner marks crowd the text. It is still a centred copy of the original shrunk into a strip rather than a real banner layout, the empty photo areas on each side carry no message, and the small text is borderline at this size.

A: the photo is cropped hard to a pixelated face, and the headline is shrunk to a small block in the middle, so the hierarchy is weak. The doodles are tiny and scattered, the molecule is cut off at the right edge, a doodle is clipped on the left, and there is a large empty right half. Still, nothing collides and the text is readable. B: the large 'HOW IT WORKS?' headline sits directly on the face and mouth, and the arrow, question-mark and atom doodles pile up on the cheek. The subtitle floats top-right, away from its headline, which breaks the reading order. These are serious collisions, so it is unusable.

A: the photo is cropped to just a mouth and cheek, and the bulb, question-mark, atom and arrow doodles are piled on top of the face, which looks like an unintended collision. Its large headline with the subtitle beside it does read well left to right. B: the same unflattering mouth crop, but the doodles sit in clear space beside the text, which is cleaner. Its downsides are a much smaller stacked headline, a clipped arrow on the left edge and a molecule cut off at the right edge, plus a large empty grey gap between the text and the molecule.

Both are 320x50 crops of the photo with the 'Perfect Taste' lockup shrunk to a tiny two-line stack. The gold leaf wreath is effectively lost, and the fig is cropped into unreadable fragments, so neither reads as a left-to-right banner. A's title is slightly larger and sits on a clear centre axis, while B's is smaller, set off-centre at an arbitrary spot, harder to read against the busy blurred background, and leaves the right half to cropped fruit.

A: the icon row is cropped against the top edge, and 'IT'S TIME FOR THEM TO BECOME REAL' sits right up against 'GAMES', so two headlines compete side by side. The body copy and URL float in a column with arbitrary offsets, and there is dead space under the left block. B reads clearly left to right (icons, then headline, then copy) with a strong headline, but the event details and URL are shrunk to illegible micro-text. The pink subcopy has an awkward 'VIRTUAL' orphan line, and the right column is jammed against the edge.

A: the forest background never stretched to fill the banner and sits as a narrow center strip. The huge white headline overflows it onto white, so only 'Devot/onal Da/sts' can be read. 'March 21', the subhead and the quote are invisible or gone, and a stray rule floats on the right. B is just as broken: the same narrow strip, with the headline, subhead and body copy cut into fragments ('ed', 'y', 'Joint celeb', 'Investing in fo'). The white text spills onto white, and the cream rules and 'March 21' float in empty space with no hierarchy. A wins only because its headline is still the dominant element.

A keeps the original's structure: brown owl at far left, eyebrow, headline, blue owl at right. But the left owl is shrunk to an unreadable sliver jammed against the edge, 'EVENT MANAGMENT' is tiny, and the two-line headline is crammed into the 50px height. B pushes the eyebrow to the far left, away from the headline it introduces, and wedges the brown owl between them so it nearly touches 'KIDS'. Confetti sits behind the text, which makes the ordering and grouping worse than A's.

A is just the original banner shrunk into a thin strip across the middle of the tall canvas, with about 70% of it left as dead white space above and below. The dark title panel covers almost all of the pattern, so the brand imagery is mostly hidden, but the headline is still readable on its dark plate. B breaks the design apart: the dark panel sits empty with no text, the pattern strip floats on its own, and the headline has moved into a thin gold outline box at the bottom on white, where it is low-contrast and cut off from its backing. The result is three disconnected fragments with no clear focal point and no longer the same design.

A breaks the composition. The two text pairs are staggered at arbitrary x positions, the divider line sits beside 'When Life Is Great' when it should separate the two pairs, and the rose is cut off by a hard vertical edge at mid-canvas, leaving the whole right and lower-right half empty. B keeps the original's order, centring and divider, but it is just the narrow original column dropped into the middle of a wide canvas: the rose strip has visible straight crop edges, the wide side margins are empty, and the text is small for the format. It is not rearranged for the new shape, but it is coherent and on brand.

A breaks the message: the lines read PRAY / When Life Is Great / When Life Is Rough / PRAY, so the couplet is out of order and makes no sense. Its text is small and mixes left and centred alignment, and the divider sits alone at the bottom with no link to the copy, although the rose is large and kept in proportion. B keeps the reading order, but its text blocks are staggered with no shared axis and the divider is jammed beside 'When Life Is Great' instead of separating the two halves. The rose is crammed into the bottom-left corner and cut by the left edge, leaving the whole bottom-right quadrant empty, which makes the layout lopsided.

A keeps the original reading order (FAMILY DAYS OUT IN → London → tagline) in one left-hand stack, but the background photo is badly upscaled and blurry. The translucent panel is gone, so the dark text sits straight on a busy city image, and the chevrons are scattered: one set jams against 'London' and the other floats alone at the far right. The middle and right of the banner are dead photo. B breaks the hierarchy: 'London' sits above its own lead-in 'FAMILY DAYS OUT IN', which shrinks to tiny text in the middle. The chevrons pile into one oversized, overlapping arrow cluster along the bottom edge. The tagline is tiny and stranded at the right on a busy background, so all the text is scattered with no shared alignment.

A is broken: the chevrons are blown up into huge black shapes that dominate the canvas, 'FAMILY DAYS OUT IN' has fallen far below 'London' at a tiny size, so the headline reads out of order, and the translucent panel is left floating loose behind no text. B keeps the original reading order and the scale of each element, but it drops the panel, so the dark text sits straight on a busy, blurry, low-contrast photo. The copy is also bunched as a small cluster left of centre, and the '<<<' chevrons drift off to the side.

A: the hero photo of praying hands is gone, apart from a broken black L-shaped strip with a white text panel covering it. The cloud shapes float as white-on-white outlines on the left, so the composition looks shattered. B: the photo is lost completely, leaving an orphaned black bar cut off at the top edge and faint cross and cloud remnants on the left. Its quote and attribution are at least cleanly centred and readable with clear hierarchy, so it is less broken, though still not the same design.

A: the enlarged headline spills out of the image band and "the limit" sits right on the busy striped building photo. That is a clear text-on-busy-image collision, and the type also crowds the top while the bottom third of the canvas is empty. B: the headline stays clear of the photo, but it re-wraps with "us." orphaned on its own line. The original is still a thin strip in the middle of the canvas with dead space above and below, so the design was shrunk onto the new size, not rearranged for it. Even so, B is the less broken of the two.

A just drops the original banner strip into the middle of the portrait canvas without rearranging it: roughly 55% of the canvas is dead white space above and below, and the headline's top edge crowds the bottom of the image band ('Sky' clips into it). B does rearrange it, with a large right-aligned headline that dominates and fills the format, but the five-line stack leaves 'not' and 'the' as one-word lines. The building image is also shrunk to a small sliver pinned to the left edge, sitting behind the headline's lines, and the top-left of the canvas is empty.

A keeps the logo lockup and the photo strip intact, but crams everything into the top quarter. The lockup is small, the photo is a squashed sliver, and roughly 70% of the canvas below is empty navy with only a stray dot cluster in it. B stacks the lockup large at the bottom, so it fills the tall format and reads well. But its dot-grid decorations are blown up into huge, blurry, pixelated arrow and star shapes that dominate the top. The photo has shrunk to a nearly invisible dash, so the key imagery is lost. Both are broken; B is slightly less bad because the brand is prominent and the space is used.

A keeps the original's centred wordmark, tagline and mirrored illustration clusters with clean gaps; its only flaws are that the art clusters sit low, leaving a slightly empty band at the top, and the art is a little small for the taller canvas. In B the headline is oversized, so 'CLAYTONI' runs into the pink and purple shapes on both sides, and 'CREATIVE AGENCY' presses against the pink shape. Text placed on the busy illustration is a clear collision.

A has no collisions, but the illustration clusters are shrunk to tiny edge decorations, which makes the original artwork trivial. They leave a dead middle band that splits 'CLAYTONI' from 'CREATIVE AGENCY', and the headline is jammed near the top edge. B has the same tiny illustrations, but the 'CLAYTONI' headline sits directly on top of them, so the letters collide with busy artwork and both legibility and intent suffer.

A: the photo is shrunk to a small thumbnail on the far left and the headline sits in three cramped centred lines, which leaves the right ~40% of the banner empty. The white heart motif has nearly vanished behind the text, so the layout is lopsided and loses the original's signature shape. B: it spreads across the width better, but the heart shape has come loose from the copy and sits as an empty, faintly outlined blank between the photo and the headline, which looks like a rendering bug. The URL is also stranded as a tiny fragment at the right edge, so there are three disconnected pieces and no clear grouping. Both are weak; A is marginally less broken.

A keeps the reading order TRAVEL–MAKEUP–KIT, but KIT has lost its white bar and sits on the busy photo, jammed against the MAKEUP bar, the bars are cut off at the edges, the text is tiny and none of it has the original's stacked emphasis. B scrambles the message to MAKEUP–TRAVEL, and KIT is pushed into the right corner, clipped and dark on a busy powder image, so it is nearly unreadable.

A reads left to right as a banner should (symbols, headline, copy column), but the symbols are jammed against the headline, the pink subhead wraps badly with 'VIRTUAL' orphaned on its own line, and the event details and URL are shrunk to illegible micro-text. B is disorganised: the symbols are pushed against the top edge and hang over the tagline, the headline runs almost into 'IT'S TIME FOR THEM…' with no gutter, the pink subhead nearly touches the bottom edge, the URL floats off-axis, and the right third of the canvas is empty.

A puts the &/Baby Toddler/BEDDING lockup at the bottom at a size that reads well, but the dot grids are scaled up into huge, blurry, pixelated star shapes that fill the top two-thirds and become the focal point. The blue product image shrinks to a tiny stray sliver on the left. B is basically the banner shrunk and packed into the top quarter: the lockup and image strip are small and squeezed together, and the dot fragments sit loose mid-canvas. The bottom ~60% is empty navy, so it does not suit the tall format.

A keeps the brand-headline-subcopy order in a left column with the photo on the right, but it is cramped: logo, gifts and URL are crowded against the left edge, the stars are oversized and float apart from 'Only this Christmas', the divider lines are ragged, and the URL is tiny. B is broken: the subcopy 'with your next cup of coffee' is far bigger than the headline and sits right on the busy sweater and mug photo, dashed lines and stars run over the image, the URL and 'Only this Christmas' are tiny and placed on the photo, and the left half is mostly empty.

A is not a resize at all. It is the original shrunk and centred, with large empty white areas on both sides, and 'EVERYONE IS WELCOME!' becomes tiny, hard-to-read text. B rearranges properly into a banner, with the photo on the left and a clear, readable headline and subhead on the right, but it has flaws. The cloud shape that blended into the photo is now a faint grey outline that looks like an artefact. The photo sits against the left edge with uneven gaps above and below. The right half reads as plain white with no link to the photo.

A: the red T is pushed into the top half and stops short of the right and bottom edges, so it loses the original's bleed and leaves about 40% of the canvas as empty blue below the stem; the layout looks top-heavy and unfinished. B: the crossbar bleeds off the right edge as in the original and the block sits more centrally, but the stem still ends well above the bottom edge (no bleed), leaving a dead blue band at the bottom and a smaller one at the top. The text sits only partly on the red, the same as the original, so neither candidate fixes that.

A keeps the original's order and readable sizes, but the orange headline is pushed far right and no longer lines up with the centred column under it. It is also a narrow centred stack in a wide banner, so the sides are dead space and the bottom text sits tight to the bottom edge. B scatters the copy into arbitrary spots: the headline is top-left, a dash rule floats alone and the body text is stranded bottom-left. The divider is broken into two uneven dash rows jammed beside the teal line, the booking/contact text is shrunk until you can't read it, and big empty patches make it look unplanned.

A reflows the copy left to right, but the maroon panel is a leftover stub on the far left. 'MARKETING FUTURE' spills off the panel onto the busy grey table photo, where its contrast is weak, and 'Join WADE team' floats over the photo with no backing. The decorative X and circle marks are gone. B just shrinks the original panel into a tiny centred box: the headline, 'WE CREATE' and the CTA are microscopic and unreadable at 320x50, and the panel fills only a fraction of the width, so the banner is mostly cropped photo.

A breaks the message: DISCOUNT sits at the top and MERRY at the very bottom, so it reads 'Discount… Merry', and a large dead band in the middle leaves the illustrations jammed into top and bottom rows. B keeps MERRY above DISCOUNT and keeps the scattered-character feel of the original, but the headline sits off-centre to the left with the red monster and holly crowding its right edge, and the small characters and gifts in the bottom cluster overlap and press against the canvas edge.

A breaks the headline: the 'MERRY' lettering is shrunk to a tiny strip at the very bottom, below 'DISCOUNT' and colliding with the tree. That reverses the reading order and buries the hero type. The gift box also sits on the moose's antlers, and there is a large empty band between the clusters. B keeps 'MERRY' above 'DISCOUNT' at a readable size in the centre, but its illustrations are crammed into the top and bottom clusters with collisions: the bell and holly overlap the heart and the red monster, the bottom monsters pile into each other, and the star monster is jammed against the bottom edge. There is also dead space beside the ghost.

A blows the small cross icon up into a huge, blurry blue cross that dominates the middle of the banner, leaving it heavily pixelated and destroying the hierarchy. A also scatters the pieces: the dates are tiny and pinned to the top edge, 'Worship & Bible Study' floats on its own, and the invite copy sits far below the headline. B keeps the original elements at their proper scale and reads left to right with the illustration on the right, but it is cramped: the invite line runs into the cross and the 'Worship' text, the small dates are left-aligned while the headline is centred, the illustration is cut off at the bottom, and there is dead space on the left.

A keeps the photo as the main image above a readable quote, but the top-left quote mark is too big and the G.M. Allen box is pushed right, out of line with the quote's left edge, leaving dead space on the right. B shrinks the photo to a small thumbnail and puts a huge dark quote-mark block beside it that pulls more attention than the image, so the hierarchy is wrong and the key imagery barely registers.

A: the headline sits flush against the left canvas edge with no margin, and the translucent grey band behind it covers only the top line. The two info boxes are staggered on the right and run off the right edge, which leaves the lower-left of the canvas as empty dead space over a blurry, over-zoomed photo. B has a consistent left margin, and the headline lines up with the blue box, which makes a clear top-to-bottom stack. Its flaws are an orphaned empty grey bar floating above the headline, which looks like an artifact, and blue and black boxes with mismatched tops and heights; the black box's text is also cramped against its padding.

A keeps the original structure: the headline sits top-left and both info boxes are stacked on the right with readable text. Its flaws: 'FESTIVAL' is left on its own line as an orphan, the boxes run flush against the right edge, and the headline sits over a busy interior photo. B wraps the headline into four ragged lines and leaves the top third as empty photo. It also puts the two boxes side by side at the bottom with clashing text sizes: the blue box's date copy is tiny and hard to read, while the black box's copy is much larger, so the hierarchy between them breaks down.

A is the original banner scaled into a thin middle strip, leaving huge empty white areas above and below on the portrait canvas. The pattern is cropped to a narrow band hidden behind an oversized dark panel, but the headline stays readable and on brand. B splits the design apart: the headline sits in a small, faint outlined box floating above, away from its dark panel, which is left as a large empty block with nothing in it. The text is tiny, the hierarchy is gone, and the pattern is cut off, so B is unusable.

A shrinks the whole composition into a small center strip, leaving large blank white areas on both sides, and the gold headline is tiny at banner size. It is still intact: the text sits on its dark panel over the pattern, as in the original. B breaks the design apart. The dark panel is now an empty rounded box on the left, and the headline sits on plain white inside a stray gold outline box on the right, where gold on white has weak contrast. The pattern is squeezed into a middle sliver, and the panel/frame layering that made the original work is gone.

A: the whole text block is tiny for a 768 square (the 'London' headline is only about 1/5 of the width, and the italic tagline is barely readable). It floats in a narrow translucent band over a busy skyline, with large dead areas around it, so it reads as the skyscraper layout shrunk into the middle rather than a re-layout for the new shape. B: the type is larger and more readable and the hierarchy is clearer. But the cluster is pushed left of the translucent band, the '<<<' chevrons float far off to the right beside the skyline and are cut off from the text, and the tagline sits straight on busy buildings with weak contrast. Both lose the Tower Bridge imagery. B wins narrowly on legibility.

A: the praying-hands photo, the design's key image, is gone. All that's left is a black sliver at the top centre and a black vertical strip running down the left edge of the quote block. Faint white cloud outlines float in a dead white void on the left, and the quote is small and pushed to the right. B also loses the photo. It leaves an orphan black rectangle above the headline and a huge faint cross outline that dominates the empty left half, and the MAHATMA GANDHI line is jammed against the bottom edge. Its quote is bigger and reads more clearly, so it is slightly less broken, but neither keeps the original design.

A: the robot vacuum is cropped into an unrecognisable dark blob, the thin outline frame floats with no purpose in the middle, and the headline is tiny for a 768px banner. Still, the purple shape sits in the bottom-left corner and is cut off by the canvas edges the way the original's circle is, so it reads left to right. B has the same bad crop, plus the purple shape stops in a hard vertical edge, the 'Smart Home' text is even smaller and close to unreadable, and the dot grids are scattered over the product, so it looks more arbitrary.

A keeps 'Smart Home / GADGETS' legible in white at right on a dark crop of the robot photo, with a clear headline size step and left-to-right reading. But the purple circle, the brand's main colour, is cut down to a meaningless sliver in the bottom-left corner, and the frame line and dot pattern are gone, so it reads as a cropped photo with text dropped on it. B shrinks the purple circle to a tiny blob in the middle of the banner, and the text inside it is too small to read. The rest of the canvas is an unreadable dark photo crop, with no headline hierarchy and no usable message.

Both lose the headline 'We help choosing the right smartphone', the URL and the HO SMART wordmark entirely, so neither carries any message. A puts an empty blue block at the top and a pale outline logo floating white-on-white below it, leaves a large dead middle and crops the photo strip off the left and bottom edges. B is the original banner shrunk into a thin strip across the middle, with a tiny, barely visible logo above it on white and about 75% of the canvas empty. That is a shrunk copy, not a rearrangement. A is marginally less bad because it at least spreads its elements across the portrait format.

Both lose every piece of text: the headline 'We help choosing the right smartphone', the URL and the 'HO SMART' wordmark are gone. A's blue panel at the top is empty, and its white-outline logo sits on white, so it is nearly invisible. Its diagonal stripes are misplaced over the photo, and the bottom 60% of the canvas is dead space. B just shrinks the original banner into a thin strip in the middle of a blank tall canvas, with a tiny, low-contrast logo floating above it. B is a squashed copy rather than a rearrangement and is mostly empty. A is marginally less bad because it at least stacks the elements vertically and shows the logo at a usable size.

A does rearrange the layout: the image band sits on top, with larger &/Baby Toddler/BEDDING lockup below. But everything is packed into the top 45% and the bottom half is empty, the top dot grid sits on the photo, and the lockup is off-centre with ragged alignment to the image. B is just the original leaderboard banner shrunk into a thin strip across the middle of the square. More than 70% of the canvas is empty, the type is small, and the dot grids crowd the edges, so it is a letterboxed copy rather than a resize.

Both shrink the illustrations to a tiny strip in the middle, leaving huge empty navy areas and losing the original's vivid framing art. A: the headline is modest, the top third is empty, and 'CREATIVE AGENCY' is small and stranded far below, cut off from the brand name. B: the headline is a bold top band (though it almost touches the side margins) and the tagline anchors the bottom, so it reads as a deliberate top/bottom poster frame with stronger type, but the middle is still a dead void with scattered fragments.

A rearranges the design into a real banner, photo left and a large readable headline right. But the cloud shapes are now faint grey outlines floating on white, stray sparkles drift around, the photo sits flush against the left edge with uneven top and bottom margins, and a sparkle cross collides with the hands. B is just the original shrunk into a centre column with large dead white areas on both sides, and 'EVERYONE IS WELCOME!' is tiny and barely legible, so it ignores the banner format.

A just shrinks the original's centered maroon panel into a tiny tile in the middle of the strip, so the headline, 'WE CREATE' and 'Join WADE team' are microscopic and unreadable, and most of the banner is just photo. B does rearrange things left to right and the headline is legible, but the maroon panel shrinks to a small block behind 'WE CREATE'. 'MARKETING FUTURE' half-straddles the panel edge and sits on the busy photo, 'Join WADE team' sits on the photo too with weak contrast, and the X/O decorations are gone, so it is clearly flawed but usable.

A: the translucent grey band has come loose from the headline and floats empty above it like a leftover artifact. The blue box is shorter than the black box next to it and its text runs almost to its right edge. The bottom of the canvas is dead space, and the crop drops the original's furniture. B: the band stays behind the headline and the staggered blue and black panels bleeding off the right edge keep the original's layout. However, the headline sits only a few pixels from the left edge and the lower-left quadrant is empty rug, so the balance is lopsided.

A shrinks the headline to an illegible speck inside a tiny purple circle cut off at the bottom edge. The 'Smart Home GADGETS' message is effectively gone, and the cropped vacuum photo has no focal point. B keeps the headline readable on the right with a sensible title-and-subtitle order, but the text sits straight on the dark photo with no purple panel behind it. The brand-purple circle is reduced to a meaningless sliver clipped in the bottom-left corner, the dotted pattern and frame line are lost, and the vacuum crop is unrecognisable, so the original's character barely survives.

A is broken. The text block sits off-centre and spills past the right edge of the label frame. Decorative rules are scattered: one crosses the frame, and stray dashes float at x≈75 and x≈320. The illustrations collide with the frame and are spread unevenly with a dead gap in the middle, so the label reads as a wreck. B is better because the label is centred with its text inside it. Its flaws: the divider rules sit orphaned in the top-right corner, and fragments (a soap bar, the bowl) are scattered. Several illustrations overlap the bottom of the label. The text is small for the banner height, so it still needs real fixes.

A fills the tall format and keeps all text readable. But its alignment is mixed: the orange headline and the teal line are left-aligned at arbitrary indents while the body is centred, and the teal line nearly touches the right edge. The body copy is also larger than the headline, and the contact block is jammed under the teal line. B is badly underscaled: the headline sits flush-left while everything else is centred, the dividers and body float in large dead gaps, and the phone and website fine print is too small to read.

A: the orange headline is pushed to the right edge, far off the centred axis that every other element shares, so the top of the layout looks lopsided and broken. B: the headline is roughly back on the centre axis, but the column is still a little ragged (the headline, dividers, teal line and contact lines are all a few pixels off a true centre). Both just stretch the square layout into a narrow centred strip, leaving big empty bands on each side. The headline is too small to anchor a wide banner, and the contact fine print is tiny.

Both keep the original's stacked white-bar title over a cropped makeup photo. Both share a visible lighter rectangular patch on the left brush, the original's MAKEUP sits off-centre in its bar, and the title stack sits slightly low (more space above than below). A's larger bars and type make the headline stand out more in the short banner, though its bars sit closer together. B's smaller bars and text weaken the hierarchy and leave the centre looking timid, with little else to show for the change.

A keeps the reading order TRAVEL MAKEUP KIT, but the KIT plate has come loose. The word sits bare on the photo, right against the MAKEUP bar, and an empty white bar floats at the bottom right. The TRAVEL and MAKEUP bars run together into one lopsided strip. B gets the headline order wrong (MAKEUP TRAVEL KIT), and its KIT plate is jammed against the top edge, with the oversized KIT glyphs nearly cut off. That breaks the hierarchy, the order and the fit, so A is the less bad of the two.

A keeps the original's three stacked white bars at a strong size, so the headline is readable and dominates; but the bars span most of the canvas width, which hides much of the makeup imagery, and the words sit unevenly in their bars ('MAKEUP' and 'KIT' shifted right of centre). B shrinks the bars and type to small, weak text with large empty margins, so the headline loses impact and hardly reads at this size; its text is also off-centre in the bars, and the stack sits slightly off the canvas axis.

A: the headline is centred and readable, but the wind turbine, the main image, has shrunk to an unreadable speck jammed against the left edge, and the red, green and blue triangles are cut into meaningless slivers at the edges. B: the headline sits left with a sensible banner flow, but the turbine is crammed into a jumbled cluster on the right, overlapping the red, green and blue triangles at a tiny size, with dead space between it and the text. A's clutter is less distracting, so it is the less bad of two weak resizes.

A: the photo is cropped to just the mouth and cheek, so the person reads as a meaningless fragment. The headline is small and squeezed into a stacked block with tiny subtitle text, and the bulb and question-mark doodles crowd against it while the right two-thirds of the banner is almost empty. B: it has the same mouth-only crop, and the bulb, question-mark and atom doodles are piled directly on the face, an unintended-looking collision. Still, its headline is much larger and reads clearly left to right, with the subtitle and molecule spread across the width, so its hierarchy and fit to the banner shape are better.

Both crop the photo down to a mouth and chin, so the face and the original's 'looking up at ideas' story are gone. Most doodles shrink to specks, and all the text is tiny at 320x50. A pushes 'HOW IT WORKS?' against the edge of the photo, where it nearly collides with the chin. Its 'PODCAST WITH HARRY LEE HOFFMAN' is jammed right next to the headline with a question-mark doodle squeezed beside it, which makes a cramped cluster. B keeps the headline on clean white, which reads better. But it wraps the subtitle into an awkward three-line stack hugging the right edge, and a molecule doodle floats loose between the two text blocks. B is marginally less colliding.

A: the headline, with the atom above it, and the subtitle sit on clean wall and read well, but the face is cropped at the left edge to half a smile, and the question mark, arrow and bulb are dumped in a pile over the shirt at the bottom, so the doodles look scattered rather than placed. B: the bulb, arrow and atom are jammed into the top strip, the 'PODCAST WITH' line runs into the glasses and face so its 'P' is clipped by the photo, the subtitle wraps raggedly, and the molecule cuts across the face, which makes it a real text-on-image collision.

Both are near-identical horizontal crops. Each keeps a blurry middle slice of the photo, so the hero fig toast is cut to unreadable fragments on the right. Each also shrinks the wreath lockup into a small centred stamp that floats off-axis in a lot of dead blurred space, and its right half sits over the busy fig wedge. A's 'Perfect Taste' type is slightly larger and pushes against the inside edge of the wreath, so it looks cramped. B's slightly smaller type sits more cleanly inside the wreath ring, which is marginally closer to the original lockup. Neither resize rearranges the design for the banner format.

A leaves the white line-frame empty over the photo and dumps all the text below it in the wrong order: tickets info comes before 'Richmond High School Theatre Presents', and the credit comes last. The play icon is blown up and jammed into the bottom-left corner, and the orange tint covers only part of the photo. B keeps the original reading order (presenter, title with credit and play icon inside the frame, tickets) and stays readable, but the orange tint is cut down to a mid band so the rest of the photo is untinted. The frame is cramped around 'Pygmalion' and the text above and below floats loosely on the photo, so it still needs polish.

Both just pillarbox the portrait poster in a narrow orange column, leaving two large dark, untinted photo panels at the sides. That is a shrunk copy, not a landscape rearrangement. A shrinks the frame further: the 'Music and lyrics by Leland Carroll' credit and the header copy become tiny, and the headline loses impact, with dead orange space above and below. B scales the frame to fill the column, so the type is clearly more legible and the headline stronger. However, its frame sits tight against the column's top and bottom edges and close to the sides.

A: the title keeps its prominence, but the body copy wraps raggedly into one-word lines ('LIVONIA', 'LIAM DRAKE'), the dates break unevenly onto two lines, the cross and 'Worship' block sit on a slightly different left axis, a large dead gap is left above the shrunken hiker illustration, and the key image is reduced to a token strip. B: the small cross is blown up into a huge, blurry, pixelated shape that becomes the dominant focal point, which wrecks the hierarchy and the fidelity. It also has a bad 'PASTOR LIAM / DRAKE' break and the same tiny illustration jammed at the bottom, so it is worse than A.

A is just the original banner shrunk into a thin strip in the middle of the tall canvas. More than 80% of it is dead grey space, and the quote and the 'G.M. ALLEN' text are too small to read, so there is no real resize at all. B restacks things sensibly (photo, then quote, then attribution) and the quote is readable, but it has clear flaws. The top bracket mark is blown up far larger than its partner. The attribution box is pushed off the quote's left edge and nearly touches the right edge. The small bottom mark floats on its own, and the bottom fifth is empty.

A blows the bottom quote mark up into two huge dark slabs that sit next to the photo and compete with it, shrinks the hero photo to a small thumbnail, and leaves a big empty gap between the quote and the image. The top quote mark is also oversized. B keeps the photo large and bleeding off the left edge like the original, with the quote and attribution in a clear order. Its flaws: the photo is cropped short on the right, the opening quote mark is jammed right above the headline, the G.M. ALLEN box runs off the right edge and is offset from the headline's left edge, the small closing mark sits close under it, and there is dead space between the photo and the attribution.

A keeps the original composition intact (photo, quote, author box and both quote-mark glyphs in proportion), but it is simply letterboxed: the whole banner sits in the middle with about 110px of dead grey band above and below, so nothing was rearranged for the taller format. B blows the top quote-mark glyph up to a huge size that no longer matches its small partner at the bottom left. It also leaves the quote top-aligned while the photo sits mid-canvas, and drops the author box far below the quote, which opens a big empty gap and breaks the grouping and alignment.

A: the headline is small in a white box shoved right of centre that cuts into the pink A and the striped shapes, so it reads as a pasted-on sticker. The artwork is blurry from upscaling, and the 'ART' wordmarks are cropped at the top and right. B: the headline is larger and more central, so the hierarchy is better. But its white band slices the tan '+' shape and the pink A with hard horizontal cuts, and leaves a stray pink sliver below the band. It shares the same blurry, cropped artwork, and neither one rearranges the original wide banner layout.

A has a clear top-to-bottom order (headline, window, details) with decent margins, but the event details sit right under the window base with no breathing room, the left-aligned headline and right-aligned details share no common axis with the centred window, and the details text is small. B pushes the headline to about 12px from the left edge, runs the long right-aligned address line nearly into the right edge at a tiny size, strands 'Sunday' on its own line, and leaves a large dead band below the window, so the layout looks cramped at the top and empty at the bottom.

A keeps the headline as the dominant element and the stacked headline / window / details order reads well, but the alignment is mixed: the headline is flush left, the window is centred and the details are flush right. The headline also runs almost to the right edge and there is a dead band at the bottom. In B the stained-glass window swells to dominate the canvas and pushes the headline into a small, cramped top strip sitting tight against the arch. The date and address are shrunk to tiny, weak text at the bottom with an awkward ragged indent on the date line, so the hierarchy is inverted.

Both leave the patterned background as a strip across the middle, with empty white bands roughly 20% tall above and below, so neither fills the 768×432 canvas or rearranges the design for it. A is a straight shrink: the dark panel and the gold headline are small and thin, so the headline reads weakly. B enlarges the panel so the headline is legible and clearly the focal point, but the panel nearly touches the top and bottom of the strip and covers most of the brand pattern, which makes it look cramped and loses some of the original's character.

A keeps the text stack centred on the translucent band, which makes it read as one unit. But the band is much narrower than 'London' and the tagline, and it stops abruptly mid-canvas. The 'Save your money' line and both chevron rows sit straight on the busy skyline with weak contrast. The bottom half is just an empty cityscape with no brand content. B has the same faults and also breaks the composition: the headline and tagline drift to the left of the band, so the band no longer frames anything. The '<<<' chevrons float off to the right over towers, away from the copy, leaving the grid ragged and the elements scattered.

A: the headline is set as 'CONS TRUC TION' on one line, which reads as three broken words, and it is small for the canvas. The brick and blue X are cut off at a hard vertical edge in the middle of the canvas. The bottom row reads in the wrong order (offer text, then ORDER NOW, then $14.99), so the button splits the offer from its price, and the CTA is weak. B: it keeps the original's stacked headline and the correct order (headline, sub-copy, offer, price, CTA), with a clear hierarchy. But the brick is also cut off at a hard edge mid-canvas, everything is crowded into the left and centre with a large empty right third, and the offer, price and button blocks are almost but not quite aligned, so they look ragged. B is the less broken of the two.

A: the praying-hands photo has shrunk to a black sliver that is almost entirely covered by the white text panel, so the key image is lost. The cloud shapes are left as faint white-on-white outlines floating in the empty left half, and a stray plus sign sits on the photo edge next to the text. The quote and its attribution do stay together and readable. B is worse: the photo is reduced to a meaningless black rectangle cut off at the top edge, and the clouds and plus signs are gone. The attribution 'MAHATMA GANDHI' is pulled far right, away from its quote, and the bottom half of the canvas is dead white space. Nothing of the original's feel survives in B.

A keeps GADGETS on the purple circle, but 'Smart Home' sits on the busy wood photo, cut off from its headline. GADGETS runs almost into the left edge, and the frame line stops awkwardly mid-canvas. B is worse: it flips the reading order so GADGETS comes before 'Smart Home', and both lines sit on the busy photo with no purple backing. The purple circle, the main brand shape, shrinks to a small leftover wedge at the bottom with the dot grid stacked over it, and the frame is cut short.

A: the headline is huge and clearly the focus, but 'the limit' runs into the bottom of the striped building photo, so text sits on a busy image. 'not' is left alone on its own line, and the photo is still a small strip cut off at the left edge instead of being rescaled. B: no collisions, but it is basically the banner pasted into the top half. The headline and the small photo strip float in the upper 60%, the bottom ~40% of the canvas is dead white space, and the photo strip is cramped against the left edge, so the layout is lopsided and doesn't suit a square. A at least fills the format with intent.

A: the building image is shrunk to a thin sliver on the left edge, the headline is small for a story canvas and leaves 'us.' orphaned on its own line, and about 55% of the canvas (top and bottom) is dead white space, so it reads as a shrunk banner. B: the headline is set big enough to dominate as it should and doesn't collide with the image, but it breaks into five ragged lines with single words ('not', 'the') on their own, and the image is still a tiny strip pinned to the left edge with large empty bands above and below. Still, B has better hierarchy and fits the vertical format better.

A actually rearranges the layout for the new shape: the image strip sits on top, and the logo and BEDDING are large and stacked below it, so the brand reads clearly. Its flaws: the 'G' of BEDDING crowds the right dot column and the canvas edge, the dot grids collide with the image strip, the strip's slanted right end looks distorted, and the bottom third is dead space. B is just the original banner shrunk and centred in a thin band, leaving about 60% of the canvas as empty navy above and below. Its Baby/Toddler type is tiny and the image strip is a squashed sliver, a clear failure to fit the format.

A shrinks every element into a tall canvas: the left-aligned headline clashes with the centred body and dashes, there are huge dead gaps between the blocks, and the booking line is tiny and hard to read. B fills the format and keeps the text readable, but its alignment is muddled (headline and teal line start at different left edges while the body is centred), and the booking/website copy is set nearly as large as the main message, which flattens the hierarchy and crams the bottom half.

Both use the same cropped background and the same centered stack of three white bars. This is a scaled-down copy, not a re-arrangement for the wide banner: the side imagery is cropped hard, the lipstick and palettes at the bottom are lost, and the off-centre 'MAKEUP' text from the original is carried over. A's bars and type are small for the banner, so the headline looks timid and leaves dead slate space around it. B's larger bars and text read better and fill the height more like the original, but the KIT bar sits slightly narrower and out of line with the two bars above it, and the stack crowds the top and bottom more.

A scrambles the message to 'MAKEUP TRAVEL KIT', and its KIT box is far too large and runs off the top edge. Its background also has visible tiled seams, with the brushes and powder cropped into meaningless slivers. B keeps the correct 'TRAVEL MAKEUP KIT' order, but KIT has lost its white box and butts against the MAKEUP box, while the empty box sits orphaned in the bottom-right corner. B shares the seamed, patchy background and stacks its boxes edge to edge with no gutters, but it is still the less broken of the two.

A: the headline 'HOW IT WORKS?' is large and clearly the focal point, but the photo is cropped to a disembodied mouth and ear. The bulb, question-mark and atom doodles are piled onto the face, which looks cluttered and unintentional, and the 'PODCAST WITH' line is tiny. B: the headline is shrunk very small and jammed into a narrow centre stack with illegible subtitle text, the doodles are tiny scraps, and the crop is again just a smile, with a large dead area to the right. B has weaker hierarchy and is harder to read than A.

A blows the small cross icon up into a huge, blurry, pixelated block that takes over the middle of the skyscraper. It is now the main focal point, and the lines break badly ('LIAM / DRAKE', a lone 'LIVONIA'), with the dates left-aligned and ragged under a centred stack. B keeps the cross at its proper size, but the dates and 'WORSHIP & BIBLE STUDY' drift off the centre axis. It also wraps into choppy lines ('SPEND THIS / SUMMER IN / LIVONIA'), leaves a large dead gap above the hiker, and shrinks the illustration to a tiny strip at the bottom.

A reverses the reading order: GADGETS sits above 'Smart Home'. Both lines are white text over the busy wood photo instead of the purple field. The signature purple circle has shrunk to a meaningless sliver in the bottom-left corner, and the outline frame floats cut off mid-image, so the brand structure is lost. B keeps the correct order and puts GADGETS on the purple shape, but GADGETS runs nearly edge to edge with almost no margin. 'Smart Home' is thin white text on light wood with weak contrast, and the frame line still ends arbitrarily, though B is closer to the original.

A is the original leaderboard strip shrunk and centred on the new canvas. Nothing is rearranged, and about 60% of the canvas above and below is empty navy, so the type is tiny for the format. B actually restacks the design, with the image band on top and a larger lockup below, but it has visible flaws: the dot grids run over the image band and the '&' glyph, the image band looks stretched and has an awkward slanted end, the 'G' of BEDDING jams against the right-edge dot column with no margin, and the bottom third is dead space.

A just shrinks the whole text block into a tiny cluster in the middle. The headline is minuscule, and the subcopy, 'Only this Christmas' and the URL can't be read at all. A large empty pink area sits above it, and the photo is cropped to a sweater sleeve with no face, mug or gift. B keeps the text big enough to read, but 'GET A GIFT' and the gift icons run onto the busy sweater pattern. The alignment is all over the place: the cup is centred, the gifts are offset, the stars sit flush left and the URL is pushed against the right edge. There are also awkward line breaks ('Only this / Christmas'), which is still bad but less broken than A.

A is just the original shrunk and centred, with large empty white side bands, and the cloud's right edge looks clipped where it meets the white. It isn't a real resize for the banner shape, but the photo, cloud, headline and subline all stay intact and in the right order. B pushes the photo into the top-left corner and leaves the right ~60% of the canvas empty, the cloud shape is broken into fragments, and 'JOIN OUR CHOIR!' runs past the image and cloud onto the bare white. That makes it lopsided and visibly broken.

A is a mess: the headline and body copy sit on mismatched left/centre axes and the body is pushed off to the right. One divider floats on its own and the other is jammed into the contact line. The booking text is shrunk until it can't be read, the left half of the canvas and the band above the headline are empty, and everything is crammed into a narrow strip. B uses a readable two-column banner with legible text and the original dividers kept around the tagline. But it reads right-first: the headline sits top-right, above the right column rather than leading the layout, so the order runs from the tagline to the headline. The columns also don't share a baseline or top edge.

A is unusable: the text is tiny and scattered with no shared alignment. The two dashed dividers are stacked together under the body instead of framing it. The booking/website line is illegibly small, and the top third and right side of the canvas are dead space. B builds a deliberate two-column banner, with the dividers framing the body copy on the left and the title, tagline and contact grouped on the right, all readable. However, the headline is pushed to the far top-right and is no more prominent than the body. The two columns don't share a baseline or top edge, and the contact lines sit close to the right edge, so it needs polish.

A: the three title bars are scaled up to fill the width, but the pale translucent band behind them stops partway through the TRAVEL and KIT bars, which looks like an accident. The word inside each bar also drifts off-centre (MAKEUP sits right, KIT sits left), and the cosmetics that framed the original on the left and right are cropped away. B: the bars sit centred inside the band, so it reads as a deliberate panel, but the title is undersized for the canvas, leaving large dead areas above and below. It has the same off-centre text inside the bars and the same loss of the framing products.

A keeps the reading order TRAVEL–MAKEUP but detaches KIT from its white box: KIT sits bare on the busy blue powder, and its empty box floats as a stray white bar in the bottom-right corner. The background also has obvious vertical tiling seams. B reverses the headline to 'MAKEUP TRAVEL' and drops KIT's box, so KIT lands on the dark compact and brush, where it is close to unreadable; it has the same seams, so it is unusable.

A keeps the panel, type and corner marks as one centred, balanced unit, but it is a near-unchanged copy of the original: the panel fills only half the square, so the headline is undersized, and stray dark triangles show at the panel's top and bottom-left corners. B's text is bigger, but the panel sits high (95px gap above, 190px below) and leaves a big empty band between the rule and 'Join WADE team'. Its bottom slash and circle float far below the panel, cut off from the frame motif they belong to, so the layout looks unplanned.

A keeps the MERRY lettering legible as the focal point with DISCOUNT beside it, but the heart creature collides with the bell and the M of MERRY, the gift box sits on the candy cane, DISCOUNT is jammed against the small creatures, and there's a dead gap left of centre. B shrinks the MERRY headline to an illegible speck tangled with the tree, so the main message is lost. DISCOUNT is pushed to the far right edge, the characters are crammed into an overlapping row, and the left third is empty.

Both are unusable: the forest background was not extended, so it sits as a narrow centre strip. Text that falls outside the strip is white or cream on white and can't be seen. A clips the headline into 'cial Even / Internat / of For', leaves 'March 21' as unreadable cream on white, and cuts off the subtitle. B is worse: only 'oted / Day' survives of the headline, the subtitle, quote and URL are cut off at the strip's right edge, and the divider rules float on white. A is picked only because more of its headline is still visible on the green.

A is unusable: the headline is white text on a white canvas, so it is invisible apart from stray fragments. The forest image is a small central strip, and the subhead and body copy are cut off at its edge. B is just the original shrunk into the middle of the banner. It leaves huge white dead zones on both sides, the body copy is illegibly tiny, and nothing has been rearranged for the wide format. Still, B is intact and on brand, so it is the less bad of the two.

A keeps the photo prominent with the quote and attribution stacked beneath it in a sensible top-to-bottom order, but the top quotation-mark glyph is blown up oversized, the attribution box is offset to the right and doesn't share the text's left edge, and the bottom glyph floats arbitrarily. B shrinks the key photo to a small thumbnail and puts it next to a giant stretched quote-mark glyph that reads as a broken dark block. That block is a big competing mass that wrecks the hierarchy and balance, and there's a large dead gap between the quote and the photo row.

A keeps the full-height blue panel and a clear headline, but it breaks 'by submitting to' / 'Xavier Sport Program' into a cramped side-by-side fragment under orphaned divider rules. The tennis ball is clipped into slivers at the panel edges, and a stray frame line crosses the photo. B is worse: the panel floats short of the bottom edge, the thin frame outline cuts through the panel and photo out of register, the divider rules are lost, and a stray blue rectangle sits at the bottom-left like a broken artifact.

A is basically the original scaled down. The window, headline and details keep their places, but the date/address text gets tiny and faint at this height, and large dead bands are left above and below. B makes the text bigger and wraps the details into a tidy right-aligned three-line block that is much easier to read. However, 'Sunday' nearly touches the stained-glass window and the window almost runs into the top and bottom edges of the canvas, so it feels cramped. B is still the stronger, more readable banner.

Both are letterboxed: the 600x200 banner sits in a strip across the middle of the square, with roughly two thirds of the canvas left as blank white bands above and below, so neither one rearranges the design for the new shape. A blows the dark text card up to nearly the full width, which leaves it almost touching the left and right edges and buries the patterned artwork, so only thin slivers peek out and the brand look is mostly lost (its text is the more readable of the two). B is just a shrunk copy of the original that keeps the artwork and its balance, but the headline is small at this canvas size; it wins only on staying faithful to the original.

A is broken: the dark panel has separated from its text and sits empty on the left, while the headline is clipped ("d-Winning / chitecture") and sits directly on the busy patterned graphic inside a detached outline frame. B keeps the panel, outline and headline together and readable, but the artwork is shrunk into a narrow central strip. That leaves large white dead areas on both sides, the panel sits tight against the top and bottom edges, and the headline is small for the format, so it is a shrunk copy rather than a rearranged banner.

A keeps the headline readable inside the dark panel, but the panel nearly fills the canvas width. The patterned brush strokes, which define the brand, shrink to thin slivers around it, and large blank white bands sit above and below, so it looks like a shrunk strip rather than a real redesign. B is unusable: the dark panel is empty, and the headline has moved into a tiny white box above it where it is unreadable (only a few pixels high). The panel also covers most of the pattern.

A shifts the text block left so it sits off the translucent strip and straddles its left edge, and the '<<<' chevrons are stranded far right, away from the copy. That breaks the original's centred column. In B the text stays centred on the strip and the chevrons sit close to the copy as in the original. Both share serious flaws: the italic tagline and '>>>' sit directly on the busy skyline with weak contrast, the type is small for a story canvas, the empty bottom half is just cropped photo, and a stray stub of the strip shows at the bottom edge.

A tries to restack the banner, but the result looks broken. The blue panel's diagonal cut ends in an odd white wedge at the top right. The photo sits as a hard-edged rectangle, off-centre, with white dead space to its left and below it. The white diagonal stripes are torn away from the panel and float over the hand. B keeps the original intact and legible, but it is just the shrunk banner letterboxed into a band across the middle, with about two-thirds of the canvas left as empty white. Nothing is rearranged and the text is small. B is the less damaged of the two, though neither could ship.

A does rearrange the layout into a blue header panel over a photo strip, and the text and logo are large and readable. But the diagonal stripes are left over the left edge of the photo, the photo is offset with a white gap on the left, the top-right corner has an odd white wedge, and the bottom quarter of the canvas is blank. B is just the original banner shrunk and letterboxed in the middle, with about 75% of the canvas empty white, so it was not resized for the new format at all.

A: the blue photo band is shrunk to a meaningless sliver at top-left, and the dot grids are scattered as disconnected vertical columns, so the middle reads as random debris; the '& Baby Toddler' lockup is pushed off to the right and doesn't line up with BEDDING. B: it keeps the image band as a real visual element and stacks '& Baby Toddler' over BEDDING on a clear centre axis, so it reads top to bottom. Its flaws are the wedge-cropped band jammed against the top edge, the right dot grid crowding 'Toddler', and BEDDING sitting tight to the bottom with dead space under the band.

Both use the same broken art layout: the illustration clusters shrink to small strips stuck to the left and right edges at mid-height, with a big empty gap between them and large dead navy areas above and below. A's oversized CLAYTONI nearly touches the side edges, and CREATIVE AGENCY is almost as dominant and sits far from it. B's smaller headline floats in empty space, with the tagline shrunk and pushed far down to the bottom third, so the canvas feels even emptier. A is marginally less empty and keeps the wordmark's presence.

Both reuse the same small, hard-cropped illustration strips: the flat bottom edges cut the figures off, they float mid-canvas with a dead gap between them, and large empty bands run above and below, so neither was really rearranged for a square. A's huge CLAYTONI runs almost edge to edge with tight side margins, and a wide empty gap separates the art from CREATIVE AGENCY, but its hierarchy is strong and it fills the format better. B's smaller headline nearly touches the art strip, its subtitle is small and isolated far below, and the upper third is empty, so it reads as a shrunk copy marooned on a dark field.

Both just shrink the whole composition into the centre of the wider strip. The illustration clusters are squeezed toward the middle, leaving dead navy bands of about 170px on the left and right, so this is a scaled copy, not a re-laid banner. The figures are also cramped and touching the top and bottom edges. A keeps the 'CLAYTONI' / 'CREATIVE AGENCY' lockup slightly larger and easier to read at this tiny height. B shrinks the wordmark and tagline further, so the tagline is near the legibility limit and the headline has less presence against the busy artwork on both sides.

A fills the skyscraper column with readable type, but the right edge of 'GET A GIFT', 'Christmas' and 'www.lygom.se' runs onto the busy sweater pattern. Alignment is ragged: the stars sit flush left while the copy is centred. The crop also cuts away the woman, mug and gift, so the key imagery is lost. B is a shrunken copy of the whole text block packed into the middle third: the headline, body copy, date line and URL are tiny and unreadable at this size, the top and bottom are huge empty pink areas, and the image is again just a crop of the sweater.

A uses a coherent two-column banner with readable text, but the headline sits top-right while the dashed dividers frame the body copy in the left column. That splits the reading order, and the headline no longer leads the composition; the left column also floats lower than the headline. B is jumbled: the headline, body and teal line sit on staggered, almost-aligned left edges, and one divider is jammed beside the contact block.
